reason: The text explicitly describes the enslavement and oppression of the Israelites in Egypt. Key passages state that 'the Egyptians enslaved the sons of Israel with harsh labor' (וַיַּעֲבִ֧דוּ מִצְרַ֛יִם אֶת־ בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל בְּפָֽרֶךְ), and that they 'made their lives bitter with hard labor, with mortar and bricks' (וַיְמָרְר֨וּ אֶת־ חַיֵּיהֶ֜ם בַּעֲבֹדָ֣ה קָשָׁ֗ה). The Israelites are portrayed as a people subjected to forced labor and oppressive conditions, which they cry out against. God responds to their affliction, confirming the oppressive nature of their circumstances.
